summary: Polygon's buying guide by Cameron Faulkner explains how to choose a power bank for phones, tablets, the Nintendo Switch, Steam Deck and laptops. The key advice is to pick a bank with Power Delivery (PD) support whose wattage matches or approaches your device's peak charging speed. It also covers wattage needs for each device type and recommends buying extra USB-C cables.
one_line: Polygon's guide to choosing portable chargers by matching Power Delivery wattage to phones, tablets, Switch, Steam Deck and laptops.
key_facts: Power banks vary in price based on compactness, port types, battery capacity (typically measured in mAh), and recharge speed.
Buyers should choose a power bank listing Power Delivery ("PD") that matches or comes close to the peak charging speed in watts of their devices.
Samsung's Galaxy S23 can recharge at 25 W or higher depending on model, while many other Android phones and iPhones charge over wire at under 20 W.
All iPads currently ship with 20 W power adapters, and tablets from Samsung and Amazon haven't deviated far from that speed.
The Nintendo Switch with detachable Joy-Cons can receive a maximum of 18 W through USB-C; the Switch Lite is slightly less demanding.
A two-pack of 100 W-ready, six-foot USB-C-to-C cables is available at Amazon for $15.99.
Each Steam Deck includes a 45 W USB-C wall adapter, and only power banks supporting the PD 3.0 spec can recharge it at its fastest speed.
A 65 W power bank should likely be fast enough for a 13-inch MacBook Air or Pro or a similarly sized Windows laptop.
Reaching 140 W requires a laptop supporting the PD 3.1 USB-C charging spec and a compatible USB-C-to-USB-C cable.
Apple's 140 W wall charger is included with 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops, and one recommended charger can match that speed.
Most Windows laptops don't go above 90 or 100 W at peak USB-C recharging speed.
Laptop-capable power banks cost about $100 to $150, which is easier to justify for travelers charging multiple power-hungry devices at once.
The article was updated Nov. 17 with checked prices and stock.
